weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Theorem 2.1 is a straightforward application of existing conformal risk control methods (Angelopoulos et al. 2024; Wang et al. 2025a). Critical gap in addressing exchangeability assumption: no empirical evidence of robustness to distribution shift, prompt variations, or strategic behaviors, despite acknowledging these violations are common in practice

Missing ablations on BPE design choices: no justification for simple averaging vs alternatives, binary entropy vs other uncertainty measures, or confidence conversion via max(p̄, 1-p̄)

No direct evidence of position bias reduction: missing head-to-head comparison showing angle/distance between p_fwd and p_rev for instances with high/low disagreement
Generalization concerns: only Qwen and Llama tested; applicability to GPT-4, Claude, or black-box APIs unclear; limited to binary pairwise evaluation
Theory-practice gap: guarantee is marginal FDR but practitioners need conditional error rates; no guidance on α selection; no analysis of coverage levels sufficient for downstream utility
Missing qualitative analysis: no case studies, no systematic study of instance types with high uncertainty, no examples where risk control mattered in practice
